newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts close higher,look to BoE inflation report.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts close higher,look to BoE inflation report.

text.p: 1625 GMT - UK gilts settle almost a point higher after benign manufacturing data reassure jittery market. Gains capped by nerves ahead of BoE inflation report on Wednesday, outcome of U.S. elections. Traders say gilts undervalued on outright basis and on spreads. * Dec gilt future settles up 28/32 at 109-10.
Analysts are split as to whether George was satisfied with the 25 basis point rise in interest rates last week. Base rates now stand at six percent.
"After the rate rise last week...plus the appreciation of sterling, I would have thought the Bank would have been happier with the situation," one dealer said.
"But that view isn't shared by the whole market," he said, adding some expected George to call for a further 25 bps rise in rates to allow the government to meet its inflation target.
One dealer said a concerted push above 110-00 would allow the gilt market to regain its footing.
"It looks undervalued both outright and on spreads at the moment," one dealer said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds has ballooned 15 basis points since last week's rate rise. At Tuesday's close it stood at 183 basis points, two basis points narrower than Monday's close.
Dealers said the outcome of the U.S. election was keeping some investors sidelined, but was not the key to the market.
Short sterling also gleaned confidence from the manufacturing data, with contracts rising across the strip.
March short sterling settled five basis points higher at 93.44.
